title: A common summand for two surjections of finite free modules over a local ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal. Let $m,n\geq0$ be integers and let $\alpha,\beta:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus m}$ be surjective $R$-linear maps, where $R^{\oplus t}$ is the module of $t$-tuples with componentwise operations [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There exists an $R$-submodule $U\subseteq R^{\oplus n}$ such that the restrictions $\alpha|_U:U\to R^{\oplus m}$ and $\beta|_U:U\to R^{\oplus m}$ are both isomorphisms. In particular $R^{\oplus n}=\ker(\alpha)\oplus U=\ker(\beta)\oplus U$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), final paragraph: auxiliary common-summand assertion over a local ring, obtained by lifting a simultaneous complement from the residue field.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be the unique maximal ideal of $R$. Apply [lem-trf-residue-simultaneous-section-lift] to form the field $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and the reduced maps $a,b:k^n\to k^m$. Its reduction assertion applies to the two given surjections, so both $a$ and $b$ are surjective.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), final paragraph: the field common-complement assertion and its residue-field lift; details explicitly omitted in the source.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-field-common-section] to these maps over the field $k$, with the same finite integers $m,n$. It gives $q:k^m\to k^n$ with $aq=1$ and $bq$ an isomorphism; thus both square composites are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), final paragraph: the field common-complement assertion and its residue-field lift; details explicitly omitted in the source.

proof.text: For each standard vector $e_j$ of $k^m$, choose $v_j\in R^n$ reducing to $q(e_j)$, using the lifting assertion of [lem-trf-residue-simultaneous-section-lift]. Set $s((r_j))=\sum_jr_jv_j$. That statement gives $\rho_n\circ s=q\circ\rho_m$ and identifies the reduced composites with $aq,bq$. By step 2 both are isomorphisms, so its invertibility assertion makes $\alpha s,\beta s$ isomorphisms and $s$ injective. These are square maps on the finite free module $R^m$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), final paragraph: the field common-complement assertion and its residue-field lift; details explicitly omitted in the source.

proof.text: Set $U=\operatorname{im}(s)$. For this same lift, [lem-trf-residue-simultaneous-section-lift] identifies $s:R^m\to U$ and both restrictions $\alpha|_U,\beta|_U$ as isomorphisms. Explicitly, for $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and $x\in R^n$, put $u=s((\gamma s)^{-1}(\gamma x))$. Then $x-u\in\ker\gamma$, while $U\cap\ker\gamma=0$ by injectivity of $\gamma|_U$. Hence $R^n=\ker(\alpha)\oplus U=\ker(\beta)\oplus U$. For $m=0$ this gives $U=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), final paragraph: the field common-complement assertion and its residue-field lift; details explicitly omitted in the source.
